repeat.text: Once this perk has been taken, it cannot be taken again by any other player characters.

effects.text: On pick, you and each other PC immediately gain 1000 XP.
Pick-time choice: distribute 3 points (lost hand or foot) or 5 points (lost arm or leg) among ability scores, per missing limb. Foot or leg loss no longer limits movement to 20 feet.
You can "see" any target within 5 x your Perception score feet.
Drawing a lever action rifle, cowboy repeater or revolver costs 1 AP. Attacks that hit a surprised creature with those weapons critically hit.
+2 to attack and damage rolls with ranged weapons per rank; an extra +2 per rank on targeted attack rolls to the head with ranged weapons.
+2 to attack and damage rolls with unarmed or melee weapons per rank.
4 skill points per grant instead of 3, and retroactive points as if INT were 5. The modifier adds 1 per grant reached on top of the base 3 (requires INT 4 or lower).
Damage rolled against insects ignores their DT.
Per rank: +1 DT against damage to HP from faction-affiliated creatures, and +1 damage to faction-affiliated creatures.
+3 per rank to unarmed or melee attack rolls against abominations.
+3 per rank to damage from attack rolls against humanoids with no faction affiliation.
Whenever the GM awards XP, you and each other PC gain an additional 20% bonus.
Spend 6 AP for a heavy unarmed attack: an unarmed attack with damage increased by 2d4. You can still become heavily encumbered.
No disadvantage on attack rolls with weapons whose Strength requirement you don't meet. Ignore the negative effects of the first two levels of decay on all weapons.
+2 to damage rolls from melee weapon attacks. A targeted bladed melee attack to an arm or leg that deals more than double the creature's level in HP damage severs the limb.

+3 to damage rolls from unarmed attacks that damage a target's stamina points. A targeted unarmed attack to the head dealing more than the creature's level in HP damage makes it dazed for 8 - its Endurance score rounds (minimum 1).
The distance you can throw an object or creature is doubled.
You don't become slowed when carrying heavy objects.
Spend 4 AP to frighten a creature within 30 feet. You can't frighten a creature you have already frightened.
Long jumps clear an additional 10 feet and high jumps an additional 3 feet. Impact damage from falls is halved.

After spending AP to move at least 15 feet in a straight line, your next unarmed or melee weapon attack has advantage. If it hits and damages HP, the target falls prone or is knocked back 5 x your Strength modifier feet.
Advantage on Strength or ability checks to resist being grappled, restrained or knocked prone, or flip a Karma Cap to automatically succeed.
The first time you deal damage to a creature's HP with an unarmed or melee weapon attack, it becomes dazed for 2 rounds.
Unarmed and melee weapon damage reduces the target's DT by your Strength modifier (minimum DT 0).

Hitting a single target with at least three melee attacks in a turn gives it 2 levels of fatigue. At 4 levels of fatigue this way it is paralyzed until the end of its next turn, and can't be paralyzed this way again until you roll combat sequence.
Spend 4 AP to become Rooted (3 AP to end it). While Rooted: +5 DT, +2 damage on unarmed and melee weapon attacks, and moving 5 feet costs 2 AP.
Damage from unarmed and melee weapon attacks against a creature's HP ignores its DT.
Attacks with an improvised weapon increase damage by 1 die rank and decrease critical hit chance by 1.

Use a creature as an improvised weapon (grapple check if unwilling): 6 AP, Melee Weapons skill, crit 20 (x2), impact damage 3d6 small / 4d6 medium / 5d6 large (not huge or larger). Throw them 2 x your Strength score feet; a creature thrown into another and dealing impact damage to HP makes both fall prone. The used creature takes half the impact damage dealt to HP.
Gain 1 AP whenever you spend AP to make an unarmed or melee weapon attack. Critical hit chance with all unarmed and melee weapons decreases by 1.
Ranged weapon attacks: spend 1 extra AP to add 1 to the attack roll, up to 3 extra AP (+3 total).
No disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks or skill checks from low-light conditions. Second rank: night vision out to 100 feet.

After staying within a 20 foot radius for at least 10 minutes, passive sense gains a bonus (rulebook text says your Perception score, but its parenthetical gives 12 + double your Perception modifier, i.e. a bonus equal to modPER; see ERRATA E17).
Spend 3 AP and examine a lock or computer within 5 feet to learn its Breach DC. On a failed Breach check, flip a Karma Cap to succeed instead.
Energy weapon damage rolls get one additional damage die per rank. On a critical hit with an energy weapon, make one extra attack (max one per turn) or double the critical damage.
When you roll Combat Sequence, you and creatures within 30 feet gain a bonus equal to your Perception modifier. Affects one other creature, plus one more per additional rank.
Stimpak, first aid kit or doctor's bag used on another creature heals an additional 2 HP per rank, or flip a Karma Cap to heal double.
Applies to each player character's carry load (+10 per rank). Items you carry with a load less than 3 count as load 1.
Area of effect of your attacks is increased by half; a second rank doubles the area.
Thrown, unplaced explosives: exclude a 5 foot radius from the effect, or reduce the area of effect radius by up to 5 feet.
Energy weapon attacks can target up to three creatures in a line; a second rank raises it to six.
Damage dealt with an explosive is increased by one additional die per rank.
Explosive damage to your stamina points is halved.
When a laser, plasma or electricity weapon attack brings a creature to 0 HP, it can explode: each creature within 10 feet takes damage equal to the amount you dealt.

Two-handed ranged weapon attacks: spend 1 extra AP to add 2 to the attack roll, up to 3 extra AP (+6 total). A targeted head attack with a scoped rifle critically hits and kills a target that can't live without its head and has no power armor helmet.
Throwing an explosive costs 1 less AP (minimum 3). On a natural 20 on the Explosives check, the explosive detonates at the end of your turn and deals extra damage equal to double the damage dice.
When another creature rests 1 hour, heal half of its total HP with a first aid kit, stimpak or doctor's bag; after 4 hours of rest, heal all of it. Second rank: heal all HP after 1 hour.
When you roll Combat Sequence, swap the rolls of any number of willing creatures. Second rank: up to three additional creatures, which need not be willing.
Cooked food you make always has the filling property, and bland food becomes tasty. Creatures eating it gain temporary stamina points equal to their level.
Each other player character's maximum hit points increase by 1 per rank.
Whenever you become frightened, you can always choose to be frightened (fight).
Moving through water: 1 AP moves you 10 feet instead of 5 (ERRATA E19). Drinking dirty water gives no irradiated levels.
Sprinting moves you 80 feet in a line instead of 50.

Once per day when you start traveling, roll Survival DC 12 (+2 for difficult terrain, a route over 3 days, or unfamiliar territory); on success you and your travel companions move 2 miles per hour faster. You also have advantage on encounter rolls.

Against a creature whose type and subtype you have rolled combat sequence with: spend 3 AP to learn its HP, SP, AP, AC or DT, or 6 AP to learn one attack or weakness. Each additional rank (max 3) lets you learn one more statistic, action or weakness.
While dying, movement costs no extra AP and you gain 1 additional AP at the start of your turn (2 additional in total at the second rank; ERRATA E18).
While traveling, you and each PC can travel an additional hour before gaining a level of exhaustion. You regain all stamina points after resting 1 hour instead of 8.
You ignore the negative effects of the first three levels of exhaustion.

After resting at least 1 hour in direct sunlight, gain temporary stamina points equal to your level. When rolling damage, you can lose any number of those temporary stamina points to add that much damage.
After resting outside for at least 1 hour, gain temporary HP and SP equal to your level for 8 hours. Second rank: other creatures of your choice resting with you gain the same bonus.
The first time each turn you fall to 0 HP, you can flip a Karma Cap to heal HP equal to your healing rate.
Spend 3 AP to heal SP or HP equal to your healing rate (once until you rest 6 hours). Whenever you heal hit points, you gain a bonus equal to your Endurance modifier.
Pick-time/use-time choice: spend 3 AP to gain resistance to three damage types of your choice for 3 rounds; then unusable until you rest 1 hour or roll combat sequence.
When you roll combat sequence, you and creatures of your choice gain temporary HP equal to your Endurance modifier. Spend 3 AP on a dying creature within 5 feet to give it one successful death save.
Spend 3 AP to activate: heal HP equal to your healing rate at the start of each of your turns for 6 rounds. Unusable again until you rest 1 hour or roll combat sequence.
Purchases are cheaper by a percentage equal to 2 x your Charisma score.
You cannot become addicted to Alcohol. When you drink an alcoholic drink, regain stamina points equal to your level.

Spend 3 AP to taunt a creature (Charisma check vs. its Charisma ability check, DC = your total). On a failure, the next attack against it from anyone else has advantage and on its next turn it can only target you. A previously taunted creature has advantage on its check. No creature can be taunted more than twice.
You sell items for 75% of their price instead of 50%.
A Speech skill check total lower than 9 becomes 9 + your Speech bonus. When gambling at cards or dice, add your Charisma score to the roll.
Spend 3 AP: each creature of your choice within 20 feet gains 2 AP (max 15) and advantage on their first attack roll on their turn. Usable again after you next roll combat sequence.
In combat, Animals and Insects don't target you unless all other targets are out of sight or unconscious.

When another party member fails an attack roll, flip a Karma Cap to add your Charisma modifier to it. If it hits, the next creature to attack for the first time on their turn gains your Charisma modifier + 1. Keeps triggering until a party member misses their first attack roll on their turn.

The first time you take damage to your hit points, party members who can sense you regain all their stamina points. Doesn't trigger again until you rest 8 hours. Only one PC in the party can take this perk.

When you roll combat sequence, choose an ally. While within 5 feet of each other, you both get +1 AC and +2 DT, and when either takes damage, either of you can halve it so the other takes the same amount. Rank 2 (party-limited, one PC): +2 AC and +4 DT in total, and the damage can be reduced to 0 with the other taking it instead.
Your Party Nerve modifier is doubled for you.
Spend 3 AP to inspire a creature within 30 feet: for 1 minute it can add 2d10 to one d20 roll. A given creature can be inspired once per day.
In the first round of combat, each enemy that can see you and has Intelligence above 2 becomes frightened.
Your Party Nerve applies negatively to the Stamina Points of enemies you are in combat with, even creatures that can't comprehend legends.

Flip a Karma Cap when another creature within 30 feet deals attack damage to add double your Charisma modifier to it, or when another creature takes damage to its hit points to reduce it by double your Charisma modifier.
Spend 3 AP to command an allied creature within 60 feet; it immediately gains 6 AP (not retained or recycled) to carry out the command.

When another PC flips their Karma Cap back over after rolling a 1 on a d20 or being critically hit, you can flip yours back over too. Second rank: you can instead choose another PC to flip their Karma Cap back over.

Free drinks at bars and a permanent 20% discount on all items. Meeting a neutral or unaffiliated NPC: Luck check, DC 30 - your Speech or Barter bonus; on a success they know you and you have advantage on Charisma-based skill checks with them. You can lose your Karma Cap to have that NPC follow the party (regained next session if dismissed or dead).
When a creature within 30 feet fails a death save and dies, turn that roll into a success. Once used on a creature, not again on them until you roll combat sequence.

After another PC succeeds a Barter, Breach, Crafting, Intimidation, Medicine, Science, Sneak, Speech or Survival check, you get +3 (max +3) on your next roll of that skill. Skill Magazine effects last 8 hours instead of 1.

Targeted attacks cost half the additional AP (rounded up). Calculated attack: ranged, costs 6 AP regardless of the weapon; can target a creature behind cover if a surface lets the projectile ricochet (GM's discretion); damage is reduced by 1 per 10 feet travelled after the ricochet.
Crafting a Chem uses one less material (minimum one). You can make any Chem potent (effects doubled, addiction DC +2) or diluted (effects halved, no addiction) by using one of its crafting materials.
Heal a creature up to their healing rate. That creature can't be healed this way again until they rest at least 8 hours.
Resting XP bonus for discovering new locations is 50% higher. You can learn the direction and distance of any three named locations (GM's discretion).
You always know which way is north, the weather for the next three days, and whether the area you travel in is populated or empty.
Crafting no longer needs a workbench, but you must carry your tools (5 Load).

When damage reduces you to 0 HP, your Armor decays only 1 level. When you take damage to HP, you can have your armor absorb it: the damage becomes 0 and the armor decays 1 level per 10 damage absorbed.
The duration of any chem you take is doubled.
Crafted ammunition gets +2 to attack and damage rolls made with it, or (instead) you double the amount of ammunition you craft. Choose per craft.
If you start your turn with less than half your total HP, your DT increases by 2.
Each time you are hit with laser or plasma damage, roll a Luck check. On 19 or higher the beam refracts and deals the same damage to the attacker.
When you fail a Breach check on a computer, you can spend 10 minutes to succeed automatically (GM's discretion).
You ignore 2 points of DT when damaging Robots. Out of combat, you can shut down a robot with a Science check, DC = the robot's Intelligence score + 10.
Spend 6 AP to remove two levels of decay from an item. Usable once per 8-hour rest; each additional rank grants one more use per rest.

Spend 6 AP and two stimpaks to heal each non-robotic creature within 20 feet by their healing rate, or 6 AP and two robot repair kits to do the same for each robotic creature. Rank 2: use four stimpaks or robot repair kits to heal double their healing rate.
Once per turn, when making a ranged attack roll, spend up to 3 additional AP to add that many extra damage dice.
Crafting an item uses two fewer of each listed material (minimum one).
Equipping or stowing an item costs 2 less AP (minimum 1).
AP maximum increases by 2, to a maximum of 15 (the apMax clamp applies).
When attacking with a revolver, flip a Karma Cap and spend 10 AP to make extra attacks at no AP cost; targets within 10 feet of the previous one. Number of attacks = rounds left in the revolver.
Reloading or taking cover costs 3 less AP (minimum 1). Reloading a Manual Reload weapon: 1 AP reloads three rounds.
If you end your turn with at least 3 unused AP, you can use them at the end of another creature's turn; otherwise all recycle at the start of your next turn.
Damage from bladed melee weapon attacks may add your Agility modifier instead of your Strength modifier.
Sprinting: small barriers don't stop you (spend 10 feet of movement to vault or slide). If you spent all your AP on a turn to sprint, attack rolls against you have disadvantage until your next turn.
The first time you take SP damage after rolling combat sequence, that damage is reduced to 0.
+2 to attack rolls with handguns. Once per combat sequence, flip a Karma Cap to turn a targeted handgun head hit into a critical hit.
Shotgun damage ignores 2 DT. If the target is within 5 feet, you can knock it back 15 feet.

After a ranged hit, your next ranged attack against a different creature gets +2; the one after that against yet another different creature gets +4, then the cycle resets (starts again from an attack without the bonus). Needn't be on one turn.
Spend 5 AP on your turn for a spinning unarmed attack against 3 creatures within 5 feet. Crit chance decreases by 2 with melee and unarmed attacks.
On a targeted hit you choose the limb condition. Attack rolls against creatures get +2 per limb condition they have.
Attacking an unconscious creature kills it.
If you act first in combat sequence, your first attack roll can automatically critically hit, or you can attack up to three times without spending AP.
Allies within 30 feet of you also have a Group Sneak score of 20.
You recycle all unused AP at the start of your turn. When sprinting you can turn once and continue sprinting.
When an attack hits you, spend 3/6/9 AP to gain +1/+2/+3 AC; you regain that many fewer AP at the start of your next turn.
At the start of each of your turns, while HP is at least half, regain SP equal to half your level (rounded down).
When rolling a Luck check for loot, roll two checks and take either result.
A natural 20 on a weapon attack roll is a critical hit and the crit's damage is doubled.

+2 damage on all weapon damage. When you reduce a creature to 0 HP with a weapon attack, roll a DC 20 Luck check; on success the body bursts and creatures of your choice within 30 feet become frightened for 1 round.
On pick, gain 800 caps. Whenever you find bottle caps, you find extra caps equal to your Luck modifier.

When a weapon or armor would gain a level of decay, roll a Luck check (DC 12 + its current decay levels); on a success the new level applies no negative effects. Second rank: on a success it gains no level of decay at all.
When you or a party member misses an attack or fails an ability or skill check, flip a Karma Cap to turn it into a success (GM's discretion).
Bringing a creature to 0 HP with a targeted attack gives 8 AP; a second one the same turn gives 6 AP; a third gives 4 AP.
Advantage on blind attack rolls, and the blind attack DC is halved.

When crafting or repairing, reduce one random required material by your Luck modifier (minimum 1) and replace it with a random junk material. When consuming a food, drink or chem, you may roll a DC 15 Luck check to add one random property to it.
On a critical hit you may deal no extra damage to gain a temporary karma cap (max one, lost when flipped); using it on an attack roll makes that attack an automatic critical hit.
When another creature rolls a 1 on an attack roll against you, the attack hits them instead. When a creature within 30 feet makes an attack roll, flip a Karma Cap to turn the result into a 1.

Pick-time choice: a number from 2 to 19. When an attack roll of yours equals it, roll a d20 (optionally + Luck modifier): 1-9 target takes ballistic damage equal to 2 x level; 10-20 3 x level; 21-24 the attack is a critical hit (max dice if already one); 25+ the target dies.

The full Luck modifier is added to skill modifiers instead of half (the modifier adds the missing half; with a negative modifier it replaces the flat -1 from E7); the second rank adds a further +2 to all skills. When flipping a Karma Cap for advantage, add double your Luck modifier to the total (second rank: to the second roll when rerolling).
Luck ability checks by you or an ally within 100 feet get +3. Whenever you gain XP, gain a bonus of (5d10 + the sum of every PC's Luck score) halved.

When a PC flips a Karma Cap for advantage or a reroll, physically flick it; if it lands face up it stays face up. Each other PC with this perk lets you flip an additional time if yours lands face down.
Whenever you or any PC rolls with advantage on an ability check, skill check or attack roll, roll three d20s and take the highest; each other PC with this perk adds one more d20.
When a creature hits you with an attack, flip a Karma Cap to turn it into a miss. While you have the dying condition, all attacks against you automatically miss.
Eating a human, ghoul or super mutant dead less than 15 minutes heals HP equal to double your healing rate (once per 8-hour rest). Eating prepared human or ghoul flesh heals SP equal to your level.
Food and drinks never give you Irradiated levels.

+2 DT against attacks from animals or insects. Eating animal or insect meat dead less than 15 minutes heals HP equal to your healing rate (once per 8-hour rest); prepared meat heals SP equal to your level.
Eating an abomination dead less than 15 minutes heals HP equal to double your healing rate (once per 8-hour rest). Prepared abomination flesh heals SP equal to your level.
Robots won't target you unless you are the only hostile target within 60 feet. Advantage on Breach checks with any computer.
Pick-time choice: reduce one ability score by 1, 2 or 3, and increase another ability score by the amount decreased plus 1.
On pick, the character returns to level 1 keeping all XP, and may be rebuilt with new traits, skill bonuses, abilities and perks. Memory is wiped.
If you have unused AP at the end of your turn, you recycle all of them on your next turn.
While in an irradiated zone: advantage on all ability and skill checks, +1 AC, +2 DT, and temporary hit points equal to your level.
Each time you sleep outside an irradiated zone, your rad level decreases by 1.
Ignore the negative effects of the first 3 levels of radiation.
While in an irradiated zone, gain AP equal to your Endurance modifier (max 15). If your AP is already 15, actions costing 4 AP or more cost 1 less.
Spend 3 AP to heal SP equal to your healing rate; usable again after a rest of at least 6 hours.
Once per turn, after an unarmed attack, spend 1 AP to make an additional one.
No negative effects from chem addiction. Syringes have no effect on you unless they are a stimpak or chem.
The first creature to damage your HP on a turn becomes marked; your next hit on it is an automatic critical hit (or doubles damage if already a crit). Only one creature marked until you rest.
Lost limbs (not the head) can be reattached in 5 minutes with a first aid kit and the limb. Spend 1 minute to heal HP equal to your healing rate; usable again after a rest of at least 6 hours.
